attribution.note: Marcus states this in his own commentary.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the firm prediction, its magnitude and its imprecise near-term horizon.

contract.note: Substantial near-term deterioration is an ordinary reading. The contract appropriately distinguishes misinformation from source credibility and supplies no invented deadline.

evidence.note: Timely research provides relevant context, but source credibility is a different metric. Modest changes around the ownership transition establish neither substantial post-statement deterioration nor stability across misinformation measures.

reviews.rationale: The packet does not establish substantial misinformation deterioration beginning shortly after the statement. The modest source-quality changes and stable or declining low-quality link volumes also cannot conclusively contradict it. No deadline or qualifying conclusive event permits resolution.

semantics.note: The normalization retains increasing machine-generated misinformation as the antecedent and the mostly manual system as the target.

contract.note: Substantial failure to keep pace in coverage or timeliness fairly operationalizes the prediction. Requiring sustained measurements and separating subsequent automation protects the original scope.

evidence.note: Supports increasing AI misinformation within the observed sample, establishing evidence for the antecedent only. It does not measure whether the manual correction system was overwhelmed.
Slower initial annotations coexist with stronger subsequent agreement. Selected posts and consensus outcomes cannot establish platform-wide visible correction coverage or sustained overload.
A platform-team disclosure documents expanded coverage through AI writers. It concerns a modified system and does not establish prior manual-system failure.

reviews.rationale: Growth is documented within flagged AI misinformation, but sustained, representative evidence of the manual system being overtaken is missing. Continuing correction capacity and later automation settle neither direction. The early-resolution rule is unmet and no deadline was stated.

attribution.note: The historical cost assertion is Marcus's own.

semantics.note: The normalization faithfully isolates the present-tense cost trend. The later probability qualifier concerns exponential misinformation growth, not this clause.

contract.note: Text-generation operating costs are an ordinary contextual reading of cheaper GPT-like alternatives. The disclosed 2022 lookback reasonably assesses the contemporaneous trend.

evidence.note: Contemporaneous developer benchmarks report lower monetary generation costs for optimized versions of the same open models. This is company-disclosed evidence, not independent replication.
The earlier developer release documents reduced GPU requirements and a cheaper-memory approach. Hardware requirements and throughput alone do not establish matched monetary generation costs.
The provider advertises cheaper access to open models, but API feature parity does not demonstrate equivalent model capability or a longitudinal price decline.

reviews.rationale: The dated same-model cost comparisons support falling attainable inference costs before the statement under the contract's ordinary operating-cost reading. Support rests on developer disclosures; the packet does not establish repeated market-wide API price cuts or independent replication.

attribution.note: Marcus directly asserts the cost mechanism.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves cheaper alternatives as the proposed cause of approaching-zero generation costs. The probability qualifier applies to the separate growth-rate prediction.

contract.note: Negligible marginal text-production cost is a fair ordinary reading. Excluding distribution and total campaign expenditure respects the stated focus on generation.

evidence.note: The peer-reviewed experiments test usable election disinformation from alternative models and estimate $0.30 or $9 for 300 articles versus $4,500 for human writing. These are generation-stage estimates.

reviews.rationale: Actual disinformation-generation experiments connect automated production using GPT-like alternatives with negligible marginal model costs and usable output. This supports the mechanism under the fair plain reading, without establishing literal zero cost or negligible total campaign expenditure.
